prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The 1997 Labour Party manifesto presents “New Labour” as a modern, pragmatic, centre-left project focused on national renewal, higher standards, and rebuilding trust in politics. It rejects both old left statism and Conservative laissez-faire, promising radical goals achieved by practical means—“what counts is what works.”

Core aims and approach
- Restore faith in politics through honesty, deliverable promises, and clean government.
- Govern for “the many, not the few,” uniting the country around shared purpose.
- Combine economic stability with social justice; decentralise power; embed environmental sustainability.
- Lead in Europe and the world while maintaining strong defence through NATO.

Key policies by area
- Education: Number one priority. Cut infant class sizes to 30 or under by ending assisted places; universal nursery for four-year-olds; focus on literacy/numeracy with ambitious targets; set by ability within comprehensives; wire schools to the internet; create a National Grid for Learning and a University for Industry; improve teacher training, introduce a General Teaching Council and mandatory headship qualifications; reform student finance with income-related repayments.
- Economy and tax: Prioritise stability and low inflation; reform the Bank of England for more credible monetary policy; follow a “golden rule” (borrow to invest, not for current spend); keep to existing spending limits for two years; no rise in basic or top income tax rates; long-term goal of a 10p starting rate; cut VAT on fuel to 5%; streamline tax/benefit systems to improve work incentives; fund a welfare-to-work programme via a windfall levy on privatised utilities.
- Business and work: Tougher competition law; fix and streamline the Private Finance Initiative; support small firms (cut late payment, improve Business Links, export help); establish Regional Development Agencies; back science, design, and green tech; maintain key 1980s union laws but enable union recognition where workers vote for it; introduce a sensibly set national minimum wage via a Low Pay Commission; support employee ownership.
- Jobs and welfare: Get 250,000 under-25s into jobs/training with four options; incentives for hiring the long-term unemployed; personalised “Employment Zones”; support lone parents into work; crack down on benefit fraud.
- NHS: End the internal market; cut bureaucracy, reinvest savings in patient care (first £100m to treat 100,000 extra patients); primary care-led planning; longer contracts with hospitals; public health drive; ban tobacco advertising; create an independent Food Standards Agency; real-terms spending rises each year.
- Crime: “Tough on crime, tough on causes.” Halve the time from arrest to sentencing for persistent young offenders; reform the CPS; more police on the beat; tackle disorder and petty crime; new offences for racial harassment; coordinated anti-drugs strategy; free vote on a complete handgun ban.
- Families, housing, pensions, care: National childcare strategy; work-life balance rights (hours, holidays, parental leave); protect Child Benefit; reduce gazumping costs; reinvest council house sale receipts in social housing; regulate HMOs; duty to house priority homeless; retain and protect the basic state pension (uprated at least with prices); develop stakeholder pensions; retain SERPS and improve carers’ credits; Royal Commission on long-term care.
- Environment and transport: Make every department “green”; integrated transport policy; stronger rail regulation and a new rail authority; public/private partnership for London Underground; better buses and safer cycling/walking; cleaner vehicles; strategic roads review; protect rural services; animal welfare measures and free vote on hunting.
- Culture and sport: Create NESTA to back young talent; halt school playing field sell-offs; support England’s 2006 World Cup bid; reform the lottery and seek a not-for-profit operator next term.
- Constitutional reform: End hereditary voting in the Lords; transparency in party funding and ban foreign donations; Freedom of Information Act; incorporate the European Convention on Human Rights into UK law; devolution via referendums (Scottish Parliament with limited tax powers; Welsh Assembly); London mayor and strategic authority; strengthen local government with “best value”; consider regional assemblies by referendum.
- Northern Ireland: Support the peace process, human rights, fair policing, and economic progress.
- Europe and the world: Lead EU reform (single market, CAP/CFP overhaul, enlargement, openness, Social Chapter); single currency only if in national interest with Cabinet, Parliament, and referendum approval; retain Trident while pursuing multilateral disarmament; strategic defence review; stricter arms controls and ban on anti-personnel landmines; new Department for International Development, aim to reverse aid decline and move toward the 0.7% UN target; promote human rights, ICC, and strong climate action (CO2 −20% by 2010).

Five election pledges
1) Cut infant class sizes using assisted places savings.
2) Halve time from arrest to sentencing for persistent young offenders.
3) Cut NHS waiting lists by 100,000 using £100m saved from red tape.
4) Get 250,000 under-25s off benefit and into work via a windfall levy.
5) No rise in income tax rates; cut VAT on heating to 5%; keep inflation and interest rates as low as possible.
